svg.title: Hopf observation with a kept fibre
svg.desc: Left: a unit quaternion is a point on a 3-sphere; the Hopf map casts a shadow on a 2-sphere. Moving the point around its fibre circle changes the fibre phase but leaves the shadow where it is; a kept fibre phase accumulates the winding so nothing is lost. Middle: old sector routing used 7 of 512 bins with magnitude-only inputs (at most 64 reachable) and 43 with a signed projection, and retrieval did not improve (MRR 0.0045 against 0.0743). Right: on code-scope trees a hyperbolic key found the scope for 77.5 percent of non-root queries against 0.4 percent for a flat dot product, yet as a read score in a language model it was ahead by only 0.018 nats in 3 of 4 seeds, below its 0.03 bar.
svg.text: Hopf observation: the shadow forgets a phase, the kept fibre stores it
1 The shadow forgets the fibre phase
Sliding φ moves the point round its circle.

so the lost angle is stored, not forgotten.
